01 / The question

How can researchers create and inspect dynamic teams of LLM agents?

Why this matters

Studying agent teams requires more than running several prompts. A simulation must coordinate agents, represent a changing environment, and expose what happened. VirT-Lab supports configurable scenarios and agent roles in interactive 2D environments.

02 / Contribution & method

My contribution

I led backend development and optimization for event scheduling, LLM reasoning, and real-time agent coordination.

Role & scope

I led backend development and optimization, implementing scalable event scheduling and LLM reasoning pipelines with Python, WebSockets, and GPT-4o-mini. My work supported real-time coordination across autonomous agents; the platform and research are collaborative work.

UIST ’25

An interactive testbed for configuring agent teams and inspecting their behavior in changing 2D environments.

Evaluation is team-level work. Simulation realism alone does not establish validity for human teams.

Explore the study & findings

The UIST 2025 demo paper documents the system. The extended preprint describes component ablations, a rescue-mission comparison with real teams, a 12-participant user study, and scaling evaluations. These are team-level studies, not claims of individual study ownership.

04 / The next question

When do patterns in an agent simulation tell us something meaningful about human teams?

A direction to explore

Simulation realism and human-team validity need to be evaluated separately from software performance. More realistic-looking behavior alone does not establish that a simulation predicts human collaboration.
